descriptions.system.root.systemathic: The Systemathic language package: one core Language (Kernel) and its extensions, layered Kernel → Functions → Contexts → Deployment → Mediation → Systems. Systems is the top Language and ties everything together into a System.
descriptions.system.root.systemathic-verification: The vocabulary of verifying a design, inside the tool: Assertions, their results, and a Verification Result for a System. "Validation" is kept for checking an implementation against an exported specification.
descriptions.system.root.systemathic-stdlib: Specific Assertions: formula-based assertions, and assertions for standard terms (to be defined).
descriptions.system.root.systemathic-verifier: Offers verify: a System and the Rules to check it against give a Verification Result. It accepts only what it needs and says nothing about how verification is carried out. Rules are defined here, not in Verification (the name Rule is still provisional).
descriptions.system.root.tool: The Systemathic tool. It imports the language package, the Verifier, the StdLib and the metadata providers (Documentation, By Value). Each part is a subcomponent with a core Language and many implementations: Repository (storage of Systems only), Host, Editing and the concept editors, clients (UI, MCP, CLI, API), Perspectives, Diagnostics, Exporter, Catalog and import/export, and Configurations (Deployment choices plus Rules).
descriptions.system.root.systemathic.contexts.transfo: A Function whose inputs are all of one Language and whose output is of a different Language. Nothing is required of how the two Languages relate: neither need extend the other.
descriptions.system.root.systemathic-metadata: Custom metadata on the things of a System: a **Custom Metadata** is about one Subject. Specific kinds are provided by other Components extending it (By Value, Documentation, UI layouts, …), each extending only the Subject layers it needs. Each provider stores and loads its own metadata, its own way; the Repository knows nothing of metadata.
descriptions.system.root.by-value: A metadata type provider: marks an Entity as having no identity of its own. A Relationship to a by-value Entity has only one side: the end at it is navigated by its owner (0..1 optional, 1..1 required, 0..N list), and the end at the owner is unnamed. A presentation convenience: the core does not know it.
descriptions.system.root.documentation: A metadata type provider: a Description, in prose, of anything in a System — the System itself, a Component, Language, Entity, Relationship, Formula, Function, Medium, Deployment, Instance, Connection, Mediation. Text is by value. Like every provider, it stores and loads its own metadata; the Repository knows nothing of it.
descriptions.system.root.systemathic.contexts.compone: A box with an interface: from outside, a Component is only what it **exports**. It imports only vocabulary — the Languages its interface is written in. How it does what it does is a **Deployment** of it, and it may have any number, kept wherever their code is: an alternative implementation, such as a plug-in, is another Deployment of the box. A box with no Deployment is an interface: its implementation is undefined, and nothing relies on more than its interface. Which Deployment a real Instance runs is chosen by the tool's Configuration, unless the design fixes it.
descriptions.system.root.systemathic.functions.functi: A signature: ordered Parameters, each of some Entity, and at most one output Entity. A Function without an output gives nothing back, such as an Interaction that only informs (`systemOpened(System)`). There is no Unit: it would have to belong to some Language, and returning another Language's Entity would make an Interaction a Transformation.
descriptions.system.root.tool.repository: Interface: where Systems are stored. It stores the design only and knows nothing of metadata. `open` reads the System at a Location; `save` writes one there and gives back where it was saved. Implemented by JSON File Repository; others (browser storage, a database) are alternatives chosen by Configuration.
descriptions.system.root.tool.json-file-repository: Implements Repository: a System as a JSON file, and a Location as its path. Writing a System as JSON takes a serializer — Systems / JSON — which is not designed yet.
descriptions.system.root.tool.metadata-provider: Interface: a provider of one kind of metadata. It loads its metadata for a System when asked, and saves it when asked, its own way and wherever it likes. The Workspace asks every provider connected to it when a System is opened or saved: that fan-out is the event, and neither side knows the other. `save` gives nothing back.
descriptions.system.root.tool.documentation-store: Implements Metadata Provider for Documentation (loads and saves Descriptions, its own way) and Edit Kind for it: Describe and Undescribe, each carrying a Description by value — its subject and text.
descriptions.system.root.tool.by-value-store: Implements Metadata Provider for By Value (loads and saves which Entities are by value) and Edit Kind for it: Mark and Unmark an Entity.
descriptions.system.root.tool.workspace: The Systems open in the tool. `new` starts an empty one; `open` reads one through the Repository and asks every Metadata Provider to load; `save` writes the design through the Repository and asks every provider to save (order left open for now); `close` lets one go. Each Open System is a Target: clients start Sessions on it through the Editor. It is the only part that knows both the Repository and the providers.
descriptions.system.root.tool.default: The Host as a process on this machine: the one authority over every open System. The UI, the MCP server, the CLI and the API each reach it over HTTP — that they do is the design; how each Language is put on HTTP is the mediator's business, left to the implementation. Interface Instances (repository, providers, editKinds, listeners, verifier, perspectiveKinds, formats, sources) are filled by the Configuration.
descriptions.system.root.systemathic.deployment.insta: A placement of a box in a Deployment's scope, named, with a range of how many occupy it, as an end has: `1..1` by default, `0..1` optional, `0..N` any number. It may run a Deployment of its box, fixed by the design; otherwise the Configuration chooses, one choice per occupant, or leaves it an interface. A Connection to a ranged Instance reaches every occupant: that is how one caller informs many (an event) without knowing them.
descriptions.system.root.tool.default.documentation: Range 0..N: every Metadata Provider present (Documentation Store, By Value Store, Configuration Store, …), chosen by the Configuration.
descriptions.system.root.tool.editing: The vocabulary of editing, on its own so that the Editor and every Edit Kind share it without depending on each other. A **Target** is what is edited (an Open System, seen from editing); each has one **History**, a single chain of applied Edits shared by all its **Sessions**. An **Edit** is a change, described as data; once applied it is in a History, records its author Session, and has a **reverse**: another Edit that undoes it, computed when it was applied. Undo is applying an Edit's reverse; redo, applying that one's. *Reversible* is a derived term (`some e.reverse`), and every applied Edit is reversible. Editing knows no concept of the core: the kinds of Edit are Entities extending Edit in the editors' Languages.
descriptions.system.root.tool.editor: The one seam every client edits through, and the one authority per Target. `startSession` opens a Session on a Target for one client; `apply` applies an Edit of any kind in a Session — through the Edit Kinds connected to it — and appends the applied Edit, with its reverse, to the History. Edits from all Sessions are applied in one order; history only grows; editing never refuses an ill-formed result.
descriptions.system.root.tool.reversible-edit: Interface: the kinds of Edit of one Language. `apply` carries out an Edit of its kinds on a Target and gives back the applied Edit with its reverse. Implemented by each concept editor (one per Systemathic Language) and by each metadata provider that can be edited (Documentation, By Value). Which implementation handles a given Edit is code.
descriptions.system.root.tool.source: Interface: somewhere to import from. `contents` lists the Packages it offers; `fetch` gives a Package's content, as a System (library content is stored exactly like any other System). Implemented by Catalog Source (the standard catalog), File Source, and later another open System.
descriptions.system.root.tool.catalog-source: Implements Source: the standard catalog (JSON, HTTP, TCP, SQL, …).
descriptions.system.root.tool.file-source: Implements Source: a System file, whose Components are its Packages.
descriptions.system.root.tool.kernel-editor: Implements Edit Kind for Kernel. Every editor's kinds follow one pattern, per thing its Language owns: **Add**T (`into` its owner, the T by value), **Change**T (`subject`, and `to`: the T as it should become, by value), **Remove**T (`subject`; the cascade comes with it). Kernel: Entities, Relationships (their Ends inside), Formulas; Languages are changed and removed here, added by Contexts. Each editor's Language extends the one below it and its own Systemathic Language, so an editor covers a whole Language with its extensions.
descriptions.system.root.tool.systems-editor: Implements Edit Kind for Systems: ChangeSystem (its name), ImportPackage (fetched through a Source and copied in beside the root) and RemovePackage.
descriptions.system.root.tool.edit-listener: Interface: told of every Edit applied to a Target, by any Session, in the order of the History — so every client sees every other's work. Implemented by the clients (UI, MCP, …). `applied` gives nothing back.
descriptions.system.root.tool.default.editkinds: Range 0..N: every Edit Kind present — the six concept editors, Documentation Store, By Value Store and Configuration Store.
descriptions.system.root.tool.functions-editor: Implements Edit Kind for Functions: Parameters (added into a Function, changed — type, name, place — and removed), and any Function — Interaction or Transformation — changed or removed. Functions are added by Contexts, where their owner is.
descriptions.system.root.tool.contexts-editor: Implements Edit Kind for Contexts: Components (added into a parent; changed — name, parent, uses, implements — and removed), the Languages, Interactions and Transformations added into a Component, and its Exports and Imports, each added and removed.
descriptions.system.root.tool.deployment-editor: Implements Edit Kind for Deployment: Deployments (into a Component), Instances and Connections (into a Deployment) — each added, changed and removed. Changing an Instance covers its name, what it places and its range; changing a Connection, its ends and its What.
descriptions.system.root.tool.mediation-editor: Implements Edit Kind for Mediation: Mediums (into a Component) and Mediations (into a Connection) — each added, changed (a Medium's Language and call; a Mediation's how, down, up and place in the stack) and removed.
descriptions.system.root.tool.views: The vocabulary of points of view on a System, on its own so that Perspectives and every Perspective Kind share it without depending on each other. A **View** is one point of view (its **Perspective**: which, and optionally of which Subject) as **Items**, in an outline of parents and children, and **Links** between them; each Item is about a Subject, and carries **Marks** (diagnostics shown where they are). A View has no positions, sizes or colours: how it is drawn is the client's business, and an LLM reads the same View as data. Text is by value.
descriptions.system.root.tool.diagnoser: What is wrong with a System. `diagnose` verifies it, through the Systemathic Verifier, against its **structural** Rule — every formula of the Systemathic Languages, as StdLib Formula Assertions, always checked — and against the Rules it is given (the Configuration's profile), and reports each failed Assertion as a **Diagnostic**: its Severity, the Subjects it is about, a message, and Suggestions to fix it, each of which may carry the Edit that fixes it, ready to `apply`. A structural error is a Diagnostic of severity error from the structural Rule; it blocks exporting a Specification, never editing.
descriptions.system.root.tool.perspective-kind: Interface: one point of view on a System. `view` gives the View a Perspective asks for. Implemented by Outline View, Language View, Component View, Deployment View, Mediation Stack View and Statistics View; a new point of view is a new implementation, and nothing else changes.
descriptions.system.root.tool.perspectives: The one seam clients read a System through. `view` asks the Perspective Kind for the Perspective given, and puts the Diagnoser's Diagnostics on its Items as Marks — so every point of view shows what is wrong where it is.
descriptions.system.root.tool.outline-view: Implements Perspective Kind: Everything in the System as a tree: its Components, nested, each with its Languages, Interactions, Mediums, Exports, Imports and Deployments.
descriptions.system.root.tool.language-view: Implements Perspective Kind: One Language: its Entities and what they extend, the Relationships between them, its Formulas, and the Interactions over it.
descriptions.system.root.tool.component-view: Implements Perspective Kind: One Component: its Languages and what they extend, its children, the Languages each uses, what each imports from whom, and what it implements.
descriptions.system.root.tool.deployment-view: Implements Perspective Kind: One Deployment: its Instances, with their ranges, and its Connections — each with its What and the Mediations it runs over.
descriptions.system.root.tool.mediation-stack-view: Implements Perspective Kind: Which Language is mediated over which, through which Medium, by level from the top.
descriptions.system.root.tool.statistics-view: Implements Perspective Kind: Counts, depths, fan-in and fan-out.
descriptions.system.root.tool.exporter: A verified design, as a contract for implementers — people or LLMs. `specify` gives the Specification of a System: **Statements** of design facts (each Language's vocabulary, what each Component may use and import, which crossings exist), the **Requirements** — the Rules it was verified against — and the **Obligations** no design check can discharge (round trips, preservation). It asks the Diagnoser first, and gives none while a structural error remains. How it is written down is a Specification Format's business.
descriptions.system.root.tool.specification-format: Interface: one representation of a Specification. `render` writes it as a Document. Implemented by Markdown Format (for a person or an LLM, with stable identifiers) and JSON Format (for a machine). The Specification does not depend on its representation.
descriptions.system.root.tool.markdown-format: Implements Specification Format: Markdown, for a person or an LLM: Sections as headings, Statements and Obligations as items with stable identifiers; it reads back into the Specification it came from.
descriptions.system.root.tool.json-format: Implements Specification Format: JSON, for a machine.
descriptions.system.root.tool.python-verifier: Implements Systemathic Verifier: Rules and Assertions as Python, over the generated `systemathic.core` and `systemathic.std` bindings; a Violation is a yielded object. Run in a local process or, in the browser, by Pyodide — a choice of Configuration.
descriptions.system.root.tool.default.verifier: Filled by Python Verifier, run locally or by Pyodide, as the Configuration chooses.
descriptions.system.root.systemathic-subjects: What can be talked about: a **Subject** is one thing of a System — exactly one Language, Entity, Relationship, End, Formula, Function, Parameter, Component, Deployment, Instance, Connection, Medium, Mediation or System. It is a closed sum, as the foundation composes one: **Subjects** is the core Language; each extension, one per layer of Systemathic, adds that layer's variants, so a consumer extends only the layers it talks about; Systems Subjects, which sees them all, states that exactly one is set. A Subject is by value: the things of a System never see the Subjects that name them. Metadata, Views, Diagnostics and Specifications are all about Subjects.
descriptions.system.root.tool.documentation-writer: What a System and the things in it are for, written up for people: every Component, Language, Interaction, Medium and Deployment with its Description, each Relationship read both ways ("each Player has any number of Monsters, as prey"), and the Requirements with their Rules' documentation. Not a contract, and it does not read back: that is the Specification.
descriptions.system.root.tool.ui: The visual editor, for people: Explorer, Graph, the editors' panels, the Script and Documentation tabs. It draws Views (layout is its own business, kept as its own metadata), applies Edits built from gestures, shows Diagnostics with their fixes, and is told of every Edit by any client. Implements Edit Listener.
descriptions.system.root.tool.mcp-server: The tool for LLMs: every seam as an MCP tool — Views as structured data, every kind of Edit through `apply`, `diagnose`, `specify`. It edits the same Systems as the UI, in a Session of its own, and is told of every Edit. Implements Edit Listener.
descriptions.system.root.tool.cli: The command line, for automation: `new`, `check` (diagnose, with an exit code), `verify`, `export` (a Specification in a Format, or the documentation), and `serve` — starting the Host.
descriptions.system.root.tool.browser: The Host in a browser tab, for solo use, with the UI; Python rules run by Pyodide. Nothing to install. How the UI reaches the Host is not stated: it is an implementation detail.
descriptions.system.root.tool.api: The tool for programs: every seam — Workspace, Editor, Perspectives, Diagnoser, Exporter, Formats, Documentation Writer, Sources — offered to code, so a script or another tool drives the same Systems as the UI and the MCP server, in a Session of its own. Implements Edit Listener.
descriptions.system: The Systemathic tool, designed in itself. It is defined abstractly, at the seams: every part that could be done more than one way is an interface — Repository, Metadata Provider, Edit Kind, Edit Listener, Perspective Kind, Specification Format, Source, Systemathic Verifier — and its concrete implementations, the tool's own among them, are chosen by Configuration. Anyone can add an implementation the same way the tool does, so the tool and those who extend it are equally first-party. Connections are stated without Mediations unless how they pass matters to the design; a Mediation states only that a What passes over another Language, and how is the mediator's business.
descriptions.system.root.configurations: A metadata type provider: how a System is put together to run, and checked. A **Configuration** is about the System: from its root, it chooses for each Instance occupant the Deployment of its box it runs — or none, leaving the box an interface — and names its profile, the Rules it is verified against. One is current: the one the verifier verifies, the chosen Deployments and nothing else. Like every provider, it stores and loads its own metadata; the core knows nothing of it.
descriptions.system.root.configurations.configuration: Configurations and their Choices. A Choice is for one occupant of an Instance: an Instance of range `0..N` has as many Choices as it has occupants. The root Choice is for the System's root, and has no Instance.
One way to put the whole System together, and the Rules it must satisfy. Its root Choice is of a Deployment of the System's root: the solution chosen.

Which Deployment of its box one occupant of an Instance runs, or none: an occupant with none is an interface, relied on for nothing more. A Deployment the Instance fixes (`runs`) is the one chosen. The Choices below it are for the placements of that Deployment.
descriptions.system.root.tool.configuration-store: Implements Metadata Provider for Configurations (loads and saves them, its own way) and Edit Kind for it: Configurations and their Choices, each added, changed and removed.
descriptions.system.root.tool.configuration-store.con: The kinds of Edit of Configurations, in the pattern every editor follows: AddConfiguration (the Configuration, by value), ChangeConfiguration and RemoveConfiguration; AddChoice (into the Choice above it), ChangeChoice and RemoveChoice.
descriptions.system.root.systemathic.contexts.export: Part of a Component's API: one of its own Languages, Interactions, Transformations or Mediums; one of its children — its interface, an API of the Component's, which others may consume or implement but never place: a child is part of its parent's implementation; or a Deployment it keeps. A Deployment exports too: it exposes placements. What is exported, any Component may import, wherever the two are: nesting does not scope it. What a Component does not export, nothing outside it can reach; its children reach their ancestors' parts without exports.
descriptions.system.root.systemathic.contexts.import: A dependency on another Component, anywhere, taking some of its Exports — or, for a Deployment, an identity: a path of placements from the root. A box imports only Languages; a Deployment imports its needs — Interactions it calls, Transformations and Mediums its Mediations use, Deployments it is built on, top-level Components it places. What an Import relies on is what it takes: a vocabulary, an interface, what a Deployment exposes, or an object. Importing an interface is to implement it or to consume it; importing an implementation is to take part in it.
descriptions.system.root.systemathic.deployment.step: One step of an identity: a placement, in the Deployment that the step before it is of the box of — or, for the first, in a Deployment of the System's root. An identity is a path of Steps from the one real Instance, the System, since a Deployment is abstract and its placements are real only under a real Instance running it.
descriptions.system.root.tool.kernel-edits: The kinds of Edit for Kernel, on their own: the clients speak them, and the Kernel Editor applies them, and neither depends on the other for it. Importing an interface is to implement or consume it; importing an implementation is to take part in it, and a client takes part in none.
descriptions.system.root.tool.functions-edits: The kinds of Edit for Functions, on their own: the clients speak them, and the Functions Editor applies them, and neither depends on the other for it. Importing an interface is to implement or consume it; importing an implementation is to take part in it, and a client takes part in none.
descriptions.system.root.tool.contexts-edits: The kinds of Edit for Contexts, on their own: the clients speak them, and the Contexts Editor applies them, and neither depends on the other for it. Importing an interface is to implement or consume it; importing an implementation is to take part in it, and a client takes part in none.
descriptions.system.root.tool.deployment-edits: The kinds of Edit for Deployment, on their own: the clients speak them, and the Deployment Editor applies them, and neither depends on the other for it. Importing an interface is to implement or consume it; importing an implementation is to take part in it, and a client takes part in none.
descriptions.system.root.tool.mediation-edits: The kinds of Edit for Mediation, on their own: the clients speak them, and the Mediation Editor applies them, and neither depends on the other for it. Importing an interface is to implement or consume it; importing an implementation is to take part in it, and a client takes part in none.
descriptions.system.root.tool.systems-edits: The kinds of Edit for Systems, on their own: the clients speak them, and the Systems Editor applies them, and neither depends on the other for it. Importing an interface is to implement or consume it; importing an implementation is to take part in it, and a client takes part in none.
descriptions.system.root.tool.documentation-edits: The kinds of Edit for Documentation, on their own: the clients speak them, and the Documentation Store applies them, and neither depends on the other for it. Importing an interface is to implement or consume it; importing an implementation is to take part in it, and a client takes part in none.
descriptions.system.root.tool.by-value-edits: The kinds of Edit for By Value, on their own: the clients speak them, and the By Value Store applies them, and neither depends on the other for it. Importing an interface is to implement or consume it; importing an implementation is to take part in it, and a client takes part in none.
descriptions.system.root.tool.configuration-edits: The kinds of Edit for Configurations, on their own: the clients speak them, and the Configuration Store applies them, and neither depends on the other for it. Importing an interface is to implement or consume it; importing an implementation is to take part in it, and a client takes part in none.
descriptions.system.root.systemathic.deployment.deplo: One way to build a box: its internal layout, of one box (its Component) and kept in one Component (its keeper) — the box itself, or another, such as a plug-in package, which then imports the box. It is abstract: its Instances are placements, real only where a real Instance runs it. Its Imports are its needs, met by presence in the Configuration, never by its Connections, which are its structure, through the interfaces of what it places. It exposes some of its placements, as APIs and as the steps of identities.
descriptions.system.root.systemathic.deployment.conne: The layout's structure: from a placement to what offers some Interactions — another placement, whose box offers them or exports an API that does; an identity its Deployment imports; or its Deployment's box, to call out through it. A call binds late, once everything is built: calls may loop. A Connection never supplies a Deployment's needs.
